subject: GCP co-sell: Early adopter credit appeal for AtlasRetail pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@atlasretail.com>, Procurement <procure@atlasretail.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: GCP co-sell: Early adopter credit appeal for AtlasRetail pilot

Team — looping you in on a fast-moving pilot with Atlas Retail. Short background: Atlas is an enterprise retail analytics shop; they committed to a 6-month pilot on GCP (private offer) with intent to expand to full production if results meet accuracy/latency SLAs. AE notes: 
- ARR potential: $420k ARR if they convert after pilot.
- Timeline: pilot starts Dec 6. Procurement wants invoice cadence starting after pilot, but they’ve pushed back on list pricing for the first 3 months.

What I need from Deal Desk / Finance: approval for an early-adopter credit structure: 40% credit applied to first quarter invoice (or $18k credit against pilot invoices), with a doc-level carveout so we can publish the private offer. Rationale: higher likelihood to convert + reference in retail vertical will shorten sales cycle for similar logos.

Attachments: SOW draft, initial pricing sheet, procurement terms (they requested deferred billing language).

Can we get a decision by EOD Monday (11/23)? Atlas procurement is expecting an update before their legal review cycle.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Sales, Marketplaces & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP co-sell: Early adopter credit appeal for AtlasRetail pilot

Thanks Jordan — quick clarifying Qs before I take to pricing review:
1) Is the 40% credit a true rebate (applied after invoicing) or a one-time credit applied up front? Atlas asked for a credit schedule rather than a straight % off list so procurement can track.
2) Do we have a defined success metric (KPIs) to claw back credit if pilot doesn't meet bar? If it's purely a conversion bet, we need legal signoff on the MSAs.

From a marketplace perspective we also need to confirm whether the credit can be delivered via private offer pricing vs a separate credit memo (affects marketplace revenue recognition).

I can start pricing day-of-Mon and loop legal if we need a contract carveout.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head, Marketplaces Pricing
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP co-sell: Early adopter credit appeal for AtlasRetail pilot

Jordan / Marissa — I ran numbers with finance. Short answer: we can approve a limited early-adopter credit but I have three asks: 
1) Cap the credit exposure to $20k total for the pilot period (we should be within the 40% ask but cap protects us).
2) Structure as a one-time credit applied on the first invoice (credit memo) — we avoid marketplace listing complications if the private offer lists full price and we follow with a credit.
3) Add a 60-day conversion clause: if Atlas signs enterprise agreement within 60 days of pilot close, credit is absorbed; if not, credit stands as-is (no clawback).

If legal signs off on the clause, I can approve from finance. Marissa — can you prepare the credit memo language and confirm revenue recognition impact? Karthik — will this flow okay in the private offer process with GCP co-sell?

—Sean
VP, Finance Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@atlasretail.com>, Procurement <procure@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP co-sell: Early adopter credit appeal for AtlasRetail pilot

Alex / team — quick update per internal review: Redwood can provide an early-adopter credit capped at $20,000 to be issued as a one-time credit memo on the first pilot invoice. Key points:
- Credit amount: $20,000 (applies to pilot invoices only)
- Mechanism: credit memo post-invoice (this keeps private offer listing at full price)
- Conversion clause: if Atlas executes an enterprise agreement within 60 days of pilot completion, credit is absorbed (no repayment).
- Next steps: I’ll attach a redline of the SOW and the credit memo language for procurement/legal review.

Attachments: AtlasRetail_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf), pricing_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx), procurement_terms.docx (docx)

Can you confirm procurement is OK with credit memo flow and the cap? We’ll get DocuSign ready once legal reviews the SOW clause.

Best,
Jordan
Sr. Sales, Marketplaces & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
